name: Kyungdong University Global
tagline: A small, close-knit campus between the mountains and the East Sea.
about: KDU Global is the international campus of Kyungdong University, set on the east coast of South Korea. Classes are small, instructors are approachable and most courses for exchange students are taught in English.
Riphah exchange students join a mixed cohort of Korean and international students. The campus is compact and walkable, with dormitories, cafeterias and labs within a few minutes of each other.
highlights: English-taught courses in computing, business and hospitality
Free Korean language classes for exchange students
Dormitory placement guaranteed for exchange students

visa.summary: Pakistani exchange students apply for a D-2 visa at the Korean embassy in Islamabad using the KDU Global offer letter.

Prepare passport, photographs, bank statement and academic records

livingTips.value: Fly to Incheon, then bus to Goseong (about 3.5 hours).

livingTips.value: Halal food is limited. Carry basics and use the dorm kitchen.

livingTips.value: Quiet room available at the student centre.

faqs.question: Do I need to speak Korean?
faqs.answer: No. Exchange courses are taught in English, and free Korean classes are available for daily life.

faqs.question: Can I transfer the credits back to Riphah?
faqs.answer: Yes. Submit a course equivalency request after your interview, and your advisor will approve the mapping before you leave.

faqs.question: Is the dormitory compulsory?
faqs.answer: It is recommended for exchange students, but you can choose to arrange your own housing.

faqs.question: Can I work part-time?
faqs.answer: D-2 visa holders may work limited hours after approval from immigration, but exchange students are advised to focus on study.

name: Multimedia University
tagline: Malaysia's technology hub: study computing and media next to the country's biggest tech companies.
about: Multimedia University sits in Cyberjaya, Malaysia's planned technology city, a short ride from Kuala Lumpur. Its programmes are built with industry, and many lecturers work with companies on the same campus.
Exchange students take English-taught courses alongside Malaysian and international classmates. Malaysia is a Muslim-majority country, so halal food and prayer facilities are easy to find.
highlights: All exchange courses taught in English
Halal food and prayer rooms across campus
Industry projects with Cyberjaya technology companies
Twenty minutes from Kuala Lumpur International Airport

faqs.question: Is the programme taught in English?
faqs.answer: Yes. All exchange courses at MMU are taught in English.

faqs.question: How soon should I prepare my visa documents?
faqs.answer: Start as soon as you receive the offer letter. EMGS processing usually takes three to five weeks.

faqs.question: Can I travel around Malaysia?
faqs.answer: Yes. Weekend trips to Kuala Lumpur, Malacca and Penang are popular and inexpensive.

faqs.question: Will my courses count at Riphah?
faqs.answer: Course equivalency requests are approved by your advisor before departure, so you know which credits transfer.

name: Istanbul Aydin University
tagline: Study across two continents in one of the world's great cities.
about: Istanbul Aydin University has campuses in Istanbul, a city that spans Europe and Asia. It is known for engineering, architecture and health sciences, with a large international student body.
Exchange students find an easy bridge between cultures. The city has centuries of history, a large Muslim community, and excellent public transport to every corner of the metropolis.
highlights: Central location with metro access to the old city
Turkish language and culture workshops for exchange students

programmes.description: Computer vision, embedded systems, networking and artificial intelligence.

faqs.question: Do I need to speak Turkish?
faqs.answer: No. Your exchange courses are in English, and daily Turkish is easy to pick up with the university's workshops.

faqs.question: Is Istanbul expensive?
faqs.answer: Costs are moderate for a major city. Student transport fares and campus meals keep monthly costs low.

faqs.question: How do I register for classes?
faqs.answer: Your advisor shares an approved course list. You confirm your registration with IAU during orientation week.

faqs.question: Can I visit other European cities?
faqs.answer: Yes, but check Schengen visa rules separately, since your Turkish student visa does not cover them.
